back: The state owns most resources and decides what is produced, how and for whom through central planning.
Resources are mostly privately owned and decisions are made by buyers and sellers through the price system.
Both the state and private owners play a major part: the state provides some goods and regulates, private firms provide others.
The sale of state-owned assets or businesses to private owners.
The transfer of privately owned assets or businesses into state ownership.
Running a public sector body on commercial lines (cost control, charging) while it stays publicly owned.
Loss of state control, job cuts, higher prices, and loss-making but essential services may be reduced.
To protect key industries or jobs, prevent private monopoly or provide essential services.
A policy of increasing ownership and control of businesses and resources by local citizens.
